articles.title_orig: AMD beats Q3 estimates, as data center revenue climbs 97%
articles.title_zh: AMD beats Q3 estimates, as data center revenue climbs 97%
articles.content_orig:
Advanced Micro Devices reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that beat Wall Street's expectations, with revenue jump 45% and data center sales nearly doubling from a year earlier. The stock jumped 7% in extended trading.
Here's how the chipmaker did versus LSEG consensus estimates for the quarter:
Revenue increased from $9.25 billion a year earlier, AMD said in a statement .
CEO Lisa Su said in a press release that she expects growth in data center processors to "accelerate further," and that meeting demand won't be a problem.
"With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years " Su said in a statement.
AMD's report comes days after Intel disclosed similar data center growth, with revenue in that segment up 78% in the third quarter. But the stock plummeted 29% on Friday over concerns about weak guidance and Intel's ability to meet demand .
The data center unit makes up the majority of AMD's business, accounting for 64% of overall revenue, up from 47% a year ago.
After years spent chasing Nvidia in the market for artificial intelligence graphics processing units, or GPUs, AMD's central processing units, or CPUs, are experiencing a major resurgence with the rise of agentic AI apps like Meta 's Muse. AMD's server CPUs are key for agentic apps because they power virtual machines and can run for hours on their own. Demand from agentic AI boosted AMD shares to a record in October.
AMD's stock is up about 125% this year, but it saw three consecutive days of losses before rallying on Tuesday amid an industrywide sell-off tied to fears about overspending on AI.
AMD is also a major player the in weakening PC market, which Intel blamed for its poor outlook last week. AMD and Intel are the largest makers of traditional x86 processors that power many laptops and desktops, while other laptops rely on Arm -based processors from the likes of Qualcomm and Apple.
Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier due to soaring costs for memory and other components, according to Counterpoint Research .
AMD reports PC chip sales in a segment combined with gaming chips. Revenue in that business fell 8% from a year earlier to $3.7 billion. Gaming revenue was down 40% from a year ago.
For the fourth quarter, AMD said it expects about $17 billion in revenue, beating the $16.2 billion average analyst estimate, according to LSEG. AMD sees its gross margin for the quarter coming in at 55%, slightly below the average estimate of 55.3%, according to StreetAccount.
AMD also sells data center GPUs and full rack-scale systems called Helios that compete directly with Nvidia's Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin. Meta, Microsoft , Anthropic, OpenAI, and Oracle are all beginning to use AMD Helios in their data centers. Meta said last week that its Helios racks are up and running, and AMD agreed to invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering.
AMD has also committed to investing up to $5 billion in Anthropic, which unveiled its highly anticipated prospectus last week as it inches closer to a potentially historic initial public offering .
During a visit to Taiwan in October, Su said she plans to "substantially increase our supply in 2027." Su and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have both made multiple trips to Taiwan and South Korea this year, holding meetings with key suppliers like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and memory leaders SK Hynix and Samsung.
In September, AMD said it would acquire World Labs for $8.2 billion in an all-stock deal. The San Francisco-based AI lab, founded by industry pioneer Fei-Fei Li, is developing a so-called world model that simulates 3D environments to aid in developing robots and other physically grounded AI applications.

articles.title_orig: How malware and a bogus job interview let attackers nab $6.3B from Binance
articles.title_zh: How malware and a bogus job interview let attackers nab $6.3B from Binance
articles.content_orig:
Hackers, widely believed to be from North Korea, duped a Binance engineer into downloading malicious software that allowed them to pull off a $6.3 billion cyber heist of the crypto exchange. Dan Kitwood/Getty Images Europe hide caption
The massive $6.3 billion cyber heist suffered by crypto exchange Binance last week may have taken place in only about twenty minutes — but the attacks were months in the making.
That's according an initial assessment released by Binance on Tuesday about how it suffered the world's biggest-ever cyber heist by hackers the FBI has identified as being a North Korean state-sponsored unit.
Those findings show the hackers first tried testing and penetrating Binance's security systems back in June, though the crypto exchange was able to detect that attempt and stop it.
Though unsuccessful, that attempt allowed the hackers — identified by the FBI as a North Korean military unit called TraderTraitor — to learn more about Binance and its systems.
Then, the hackers tried again. In September, a Binance engineer was contacted in a job-hunting platform by a person posing as a "project director" from a company that turned out to be fictious.
The engineer then conducted a first-round interview with a supposed HR representative from the fake company. The hackers used this interview to "build trust," with the Binance employee, the exchange said. The interviewer even shared supposed social media accounts, as well as personal photos and videos with the Binance engineer.
"This was more advanced and deceptive than previously seen social engineering approaches," Binance said in its assessment.
The engineer was then told he would be conducting a second interview with the supposed CEO of the company in a popular social chat app. It was in this interview that the Binance employee — who was at his work laptop — was asked to download "an assignment" as part of the job recruitment process.
Instead, the "assignment" contained malicious code that allowed hackers to build out an attack that culminated last week when hackers made off with over $6 billion worth of crypto currencies held by Binance's customers at the exchange.
Binance said in the statement posted on X that the company is taking a series of actions, including an independent cybersecurity review to prevent future attacks. On Monday the exchange had said it had already replaced most of the stolen crypto currencies stolen by customers using its own funds.
"This should not have happened," Binance said in its assessment on Tuesday. "And we apologise for the concern, disruption and uncertainty it caused our users, partners and the wider industry."

articles.title_orig: Nasdaq ends higher as AI heavyweights rebound ahead of midterm results
articles.title_zh: Nasdaq ends higher as AI heavyweights rebound ahead of midterm results
articles.content_orig:
With prediction markets pricing in a big victory for Democrats in Tuesday's midterm elections , traders are leaning into a group of stocks that investors often categorize as beneficiaries of left-wing leadership. Options trading in clean-energy stocks, particularly solar companies, surged on Tuesday, despite a five-month sell-off in the group that's left most of the companies in the industry group down on the year.
Follow CNBC's live coverage of the 2026 midterm elections
Volume in the Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) surged to 40 times higher than usual Tuesday, according to Cboe LiveVol data. The fund, which typically trades fewer than 500 contracts a day the past month, traded more than 20,000 contracts by midday, and 99% of them were calls. The ETF rallied more than 400% from its pandemic low through the 2020 election before giving almost all of the gains back by April last year.
The most popular trade in TAN was buying the 50-strike call for December expiry for 80 cents and looking for a 17% rally, according to SpotGamma data. For nearer expiry, the 46 and 47-strike calls were also popular. Among individual stocks, SolarEdge Technologies stands out, on pace for three times higher-than-average volume and more than 75% of trading in calls. The company reports earnings before the bell tomorrow and rallied more than 6% Tuesday. The most popular trade was buying the 35-strike call expiring Friday. "I would only like solar if blue was in the White House," said Charlie Moon of Chicago-based Prosper Trading Academy. "But Enphase does stands out with some insider buying." Bulls were indeed dabbling in Enphase Energy , whose stock fell 20% after earnings last week but have fully recovered since and rallied 9% Tuesday. On volume twice the average, traders likely bought 8,600 calls, compared to under 900 puts. The most popular trade in Enphase was to buy the 35-strike call expiring in January, a trade that costs $2.45 per contract and needs Enphase to rally 23%.

articles.title_orig: Xbox’s Arkane Studios Attracts Multiple Bidders, Including Ubisoft
articles.title_zh: Xbox’s Arkane Studios Attracts Multiple Bidders, Including Ubisoft
articles.content_orig:
Ubisoft is reportedly among multiple suitors preparing bids to try and purchase French developer Arkane Lyon, makers of the Dishonored series and the upcoming Marvel's Blade, from Microsoft in the wake of the first-party publisher's ongoing Xbox " reset ."
According to a new report from Bloomberg, at least three companies have submitted bids to Microsoft so far, with Assassin's Creed publisher Ubisoft among them. The identities of the other bidders are not yet publicly known, but Microsoft has not accepted any bids yet. Bloomberg states that a deal would allow Arkane Lyon to complete its current project, Marvel's Blade, which the outlet says "is expected to be released within the next year or two."
Arkane's other studio in Austin, Texas, was closed by Microsoft in 2024 as part of a larger series of project cuts and personnel layoffs. The Austin team had been responsible for the critically acclaimed studio's only flop, 2023's disappointing co-op vampire-hunting game Redfall, which IGN gave a 4 out of 10 in our review . Previously, Arkane Austin developed the buggy-at-launch-but-quickly-fixed immersive sim Prey as well as the beloved original Dishonored.
Arkane Lyon, meanwhile, was responsible for the 10-out-of-10 first-person immersive sim Deathloop along with the outstanding Dishonored 2.
Four studios have been spun out of Xbox so far rather than being immediately shut down as part of the "reset": Double Fine, which has gone independent ; Compulsion Games, which has also gone independent ; Undead Labs, which has gone independent but signed a publishing deal with an unidentified company for State of Decay 3; and Ninja Theory, which unfortunately might close down after Microsoft had two deals for another company to acquire it fall through .
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title_orig: King calls slave trade a 'shameful chapter' during Commonwealth address
articles.title_zh: King calls slave trade a 'shameful chapter' during Commonwealth address
articles.content_orig:
King Charles has described the transatlantic slave trade as a "shameful chapter of history" that filled him with "profound sorrow" as he opened a summit of Commonwealth leaders in the Caribbean.
He said the trade in enslaved persons "still casts a shadow" over the association of nations.
There have been calls from some for the UK to make a formal apology for its historic role in the slave trade ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (Chogm) in Antigua and Barbuda, but there was not one in the King's address.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham, also at the summit, has said that he is open to Britain issuing a formal apology but has ruled out financial reparations.
While there was no direct apology, the King did offer some contrition - and there was also an acknowledgement that he had personally learnt more about the legacy of the slave trade.
He said: "The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth.
"As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow."
He told the summit: "The more I have furthered my own understanding of the issues, through listening, learning and looking, the more committed I have become to finding ways for us to work in modern partnership to address the wrongs of the past with action for the future."
King Charles continued: "History is not ours to choose or to change. It is bequeathed to us in complex synthesis by forebears we can never know.
"Our inheritance includes both their achievements and their failures – the good they did as well as the wrongs."
The King's address also referenced the "brutal conflicts" the world is facing, the "catastrophic reality" of climate and rapid technological development.
The Chogm meeting gathers leaders from 56 states every two years in a different part of the Commonwealth, a voluntary grouping made up primarily of former territories of the British Empire.
The biennial meeting's official theme this year is Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth.
Speaking on Tuesday, Burnham said his government was bringing a new approach, aiming to "revitalise the Commonwealth", despite turning down demands for reparations.
"I've been very clear that we do not support reparations," he said.
"But it's not the case that we don't support countries in the Commonwealth around development, and helping them with debt issues that they've got, green finance.
"That's what we've done under all governments and in my view we should continue to do as part of being a Commonwealth."
The King and Queen are on a tour of the Caribbean which has reignited difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.
On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech in which he spoke of the "suffering of the past".
In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion, where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.

articles.title_orig: Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash
articles.title_zh: Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash
articles.content_orig:
Ãscar Puente had been under mounting pressure as opposition parties and some allies of the government called on him to step down
Spain's Transport Minister Ãscar Puente has resigned - six days after the high-speed train collision in which at least 69 people were killed and dozens injured.
He announced his decision in Congress, where he had appeared to give the circumstances of last Wednesday's crash near the town of Urda, south of the capital Madrid.
"A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot remain in office after two accidents of this seriousness in less than a year," he said, also referring to a deadly crash in January in Andalusia, southern Spain
The latest tragedy in Urda happened when a state-operated Renfe high-speed train smashed into the back of another stationary train operated by the Iryo company.
Rescuers had to use heavy lifting equipment to get access to derailed carriages where a number of passengers were trapped
Puente announced his decision at the end of a congressional session on Tuesday evening in which he had outlined new rail safety measures and been grilled by the opposition.
He said he had taken the decision immediately after the 28 October disaster.
Puente had been under mounting pressure as opposition parties and some allies of the government called on him to step down.
Leaked audio recordings published in Spanish media soon after the crash revealed conversations between train drivers and a control centre just minutes before the disaster.
Three tapes between Madrid's control centre and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another train had stopped on the track, about 25km (15 miles) ahead.
Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez has said that authorities will "get to the bottom of every last detail of this tragedy".

articles.title_orig: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say
articles.title_zh: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Staff spent years warning that OpenAI's shared code repository exposed too much, and a researcher breach showed how fast an outsider could get in
Tue 3 Nov 2026 · 16:12 EST · 3 min read
OpenAI keeps much of its code in one enormous shared repository. For years, employees warned that this setup let anyone with code access peek at projects far outside their own job.
Those warnings did not lead to a fix in time. In 2026, outside security researchers showed the same repository could be reached from a weak point on the company’s community forum, and they did it in under 72 hours.
At OpenAI, that meant staff with code access could view details of many projects unrelated to their roles. Current and former employees repeatedly flagged this as a risk, arguing that loose internal controls could expose sensitive work to people who had no business seeing it.
The complaints are not new. Employees raised security concerns with leadership before ChatGPT launched in November 2022. According to those staff accounts, management seemed more focused on shipping quickly than on locking things down.
The warnings became concrete when researchers from security firm Hacktron went looking for holes. On July 25, 2026, they exploited a vulnerability in OpenAI’s community forum.
That flaw gave them remote code execution, meaning they could run their own commands on OpenAI’s systems. From there, they reached the internal code repository in under 72 hours.
The key ingredient was an SSO misconfiguration. Single sign-on is the system that lets one login unlock many internal tools. Configure it badly, and a foothold in a minor service can turn into access to something far more valuable.
Hacktron disclosed the issue responsibly, and the case involved a proof-of-concept pull request numbered #1186742. A pull request is a proposed code change, so its existence signals the researchers could do more than simply read files.

OpenAI paid Hacktron a $6,500 bug bounty for the report.
The company responded by revising its security setup. Changes included narrowing token permissions. Tokens are digital keys that grant software and users specific access rights, and narrowing them means each key now opens fewer doors.
Security researchers from Hacktron reported the incident publicly in September 2026.
OpenAI had already begun shifting resources before the Hacktron findings went public. In August 2026, senior executive Thibault Sottiaux announced that 25% of the company’s production engineers would be redirected toward strengthening security infrastructure.
OpenAI maintains that its most confidential work sits in separate repositories, outside the shared monorepo. In other words, the company argues the most sensitive material was never behind the same door everyone could open.
That defense matters, but it does not fully answer the original complaint. Employees were not only worried about the most secret projects. They were worried about broad, casual access to work unrelated to their roles.
Concerns raised before late 2022 were still relevant in 2026, and the eventual proof came from outsiders rather than an internal audit.
There is also a newer pressure on the horizon. AI-enabled coding tools are increasing vulnerability exposure, letting attackers and researchers alike probe systems faster than before.
For OpenAI, the stakes are partly about protecting its own intellectual property. Model research, product plans and infrastructure code are the core of its competitive position, and broad internal access raises the risk of leaks, whether accidental or deliberate.

articles.title_orig: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway construction making progress
articles.title_zh: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway construction making progress
articles.content_orig:
Construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is steadily advancing, with work underway on 28 of the 29 planned tunnels and 47 of 50 bridges along the route’s roughly 305-kilometer Kyrgyz section, according to Kyrgyz Railways, a partner in the project. About 22 percent of total construction work is expected to be completed by the end of 2026, with tunnel excavation currently 21.5 percent complete, earthworks 67 percent complete and bridge pile foundations 95 percent complete, the project’s deputy director general said . The first tunnel, “Kosh-Dobo-2,” was fully excavated in August, and the first bridge structures are expected to be installed in 2027. The railway is officially scheduled to launch operations in 2031, though contractors are striving to finish work earlier. Once complete, the roughly 530-kilometer line will provide China with a shorter, faster, and cheaper rail route into Central Asia and onward markets.
Kyrgyzstan announced that construction is set to begin in Manas on a new airport designed to handle air cargo. With the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway running through Manas, the new airport facility is envisioned as a key cog in a major air, rail, and road freight network.
Beijing recently hosted a signing ceremony for the Central Asia and Caucasus Private Equity Fund . The Fund is co-sponsored by the China Investment Corporation, Oman’s Investment Authority, the Uzbekistan Fund for Reconstruction and Development, OYAK of Turkey, the Eurasian Development Bank and Shenwan Hongyuan Securities Co., Ltd. The fund aims to invest in companies across Central Asia and the Caucasus, but no information is publicly available about its capitalization, the division of shares, investment start date or the first recipient companies.
The Kyrgyz Marketing Association and the Tajikistan Advertising Association separately signed MoUs with the China Advertising Association, a state-run organization. The deals seek to exchange best practices among Chinese and Central Asian advertisers via the hosting of joint conferences and forums, as well as increase bilateral investment advertising and help Chinese companies enter Central Asian markets.
China Energy Engineering Corporation’s international engineering subsidiary has announced the signing of an engineering, procurement and construction contract for a 700 megawatt (MW) solar power project in Kazakhstan’s Almaty Region. The facility will use high-efficiency 720-watt bifacial solar modules and single-axis tracking systems to increase electricity generation. The Chinese contractor’s announcement did not disclose the project owner, contract value, exact signing date, construction schedule or expected commissioning date.
Kazakhstan launched construction of the Iconic Complex in Alatau City, with the state-owned China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC) serving as general contractor. The mixed-use development, valued at more than $800 million, will include two towers measuring 272 and 78 meters. Completion is scheduled for late 2029. The $800 million represents the total project investment, rather than the disclosed value of CSCEC’s construction contract.
Ride-hailing platform inDrive, Chinese autonomous-driving company Pony.ai and US tech giant NVIDIA signed an MoU to explore deploying autonomous taxis in Kazakhstan. The companies will assess the technical, regulatory and commercial feasibility of introducing Pony.ai’s seventh-generation robotaxis through the inDrive platform, supported by NVIDIA’s autonomous-driving technology. Kazakhstan would serve as a test market, with trials targeted for Astana in the first half of 2027. Commercial deployment remains subject to government approval, and no investment value or fleet size was initially disclosed.
Chinese engineering company Tianchen, a subsidiary of China’s National Chemical Engineering Group, announced that a calcium chloride production unit at a chemical complex in Kazakhstan had successfully completed cold commissioning tests. The milestone represents progress toward operational readiness, but the unit has not begun commercial production.
A Chinese-backed green-energy equipment service center was unveiled during a Kazakhstan-China technical cooperation forum in Astana. Established with the participation of China Service Technology (Shandong) Co. and its Kazakh subsidiary, the initiative will support power-plant equipment maintenance, modernization and specialist training. The center’s operator reported that one steam-turbine modernization project is underway, with equipment deliveries expected in early 2027. Three additional projects remain under discussion.
Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Internal Affairs published a draft law to ratify an agreement with China governing security and law enforcement at the Khorgos International Border Cooperation Center. The agreement, originally signed in Beijing on September 7, establishes procedures for investigating offenses, locating and detaining suspects and responding to national security threats. The draft law’s provisions permit authorities to exchange national security information without a prior request, according to Kazinform . The draft remains open for public consultation until November 18.
Kazakhstan’s PTC Holding signed a strategic cooperation agreement with Chinese railway logistics company International Freight Trains, seeking to expand cross-border railway freight services and attract additional Chinese cargo through Kazakhstan and other Central Asian states. Chinese representatives also expressed interest in PTC Holding’s Silkway CA logistics center under development in Uzbekistan. Details, including investment amount, freight-volume target and implementation timetable, were not immediately disclosed.
Kazakh budget airline FlyArystan launched direct flights between Astana and Yining, in China’s Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. The route operates three times weekly, expanding the airline’s network to four routes between Kazakhstan and Xinjiang. FlyArystan said it has become the largest foreign airline operating in Xinjiang and plans further expansion.
Uzbek car producer ADM Global announced the launch of a $100 million upgrade to its factory in Uzbekistan to assemble new models of hybrid and electric cars of Chinese auto brands Changan, Chery, and Haval.
Uzkimyosanoat , a state-owned company specializing in chemical and fertilizer production, signed an MoU with China Tianchen Engineering Corporation establishing a framework for bilateral cooperation. The agreement covers a joint project to produce ammonia and urea based on deep-coal processing. The parties plan to study the project’s technical and economic feasibility, assess available coal resources, identify optimal technologies and production capacities and consider potential implementation mechanisms.
Energy Minister Sherzod Khodjayev visited a 500 MW wind power plant under construction by China’s Universal Energy in the Samarkand Region. Officials briefed him on the project’s progress and measures being taken to keep it on schedule. The $500 million plant is expected to generate 1.752 billion kWh of electricity annually. The project’s first stage is expected to begin operating by the end of 2026, with full capacity scheduled for 2027.
A delegation from the China Construction Engineering Corporation met with representatives of Uzmetkombinat to discuss building a 60 MW electricity storage system and modernizing the residential facilities for Uzbek workers in the Tashkent region. The Chinese delegation and Uzmetkombinat executives also met with city officials in Bekobod, about 140 kilometers south of Tashkent. There, they signed agreements on joint projects to improve public infrastructure and introduce modern engineering solutions to benefit local residents. Uzmetkombinat is a major producer of metal products in Uzbekistan, including steel.

articles.title_orig: ‘Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel’ Reveals Its Location—But Not Release Year
articles.title_zh: ‘Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel’ Reveals Its Location—But Not Release Year
articles.content_orig:
The headline tells the story: The Elder Scrolls VI has an official subtitle and it's Sentinel. So the full game is now titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, or, as we will undoubtedly refer to it moving forward, as we colloquially do with the previous three games (Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim), Sentinel.
The news comes from Bethesda's various social media accounts, which are all sharing the video above. Along with the video, music, and the title, it also shares the text as a quote attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest to High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell (4E 206): "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."
Sentinel is one of the nine major kingdoms within Hammerfell and is the capital of both the Alik'r Desert region and the Myrkwasa region of the Alik'r (source: elderscrolls.fandom ). With this knowledge, it's fair to assume Sentinel will have many desert locations.
The name continues the tradition of naming the games after locations in the Elder Scrolls universe. Oblivion is the sort of exception, as it is a realm, but it still counts. We still don't know exactly when The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel will be released, but we're now about seven years from its original announcement at E3 2018.

articles.title_orig: JetBlue raises bag fees for third time in a year as fuel costs bite
articles.title_zh: JetBlue raises bag fees for third time in a year as fuel costs bite
articles.content_orig:
Welcome to the era of the $70 bag fee.
JetBlue Airways has raised the price of checking a bag for many customers for the third time in less than a year as high fuel costs continue to eat into the industry's profits.
Checking a first bag for travelers booked in economy will now be $50, up from $45, if purchased more than 24 hours before departure during a non-peak travel period. If it's paid within 24 hours of departure, the fee will be $60. During a peak period, such as during the holidays or the summer, it will be $55, up from $49, and $70 for within 24 hours of departure.
There are exceptions to the checked bag fees, such as for customers who hold a co-branded JetBlue credit card or hold elite frequent flyer status.
"We're adjusting checked bag fees to help offset rising fuel and operating costs," JetBlue said in a statement. "This helps us keep our base fares competitive while giving customers the choice to pay for a checked bag only if they need one."
The price of jet fuel, airlines' biggest cost after labor, has roughly doubled this year since the start of the Iran war in February, costing airlines billions and driving up the price of tickets. Jet fuel was going for $4.44 a gallon on Tuesday for the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.
Other airlines often follow when one carrier raises fees. Major U.S. airlines did so earlier this year after JetBlue raised its bag fees.
The changes were reported earlier by the Thrifty Traveler blog .

articles.title_orig: JetBlue Leads The Industry In Raising Checked Bag Fees… Again!
articles.title_zh: JetBlue Leads The Industry In Raising Checked Bag Fees… Again!
articles.content_orig:
For whatever reason, JetBlue tends to be the industry leader when it comes to raising checked bag fees, and competitors tend to follow. Earlier this year, JetBlue was the first major US carrier to raise checked bag fees , and now the airline is raising checked bag fees again…
Effective immediately (for tickets purchased as of November 3, 2026), JetBlue has increased checked bag fees . JetBlue has a rather complicated fee structure for checked bags, with both off-peak and peak pricing, plus different pricing based on whether you pay for the bag 24 hours or more in advance.
Below is a chart with JetBlue’s new checked bag fees.
As you can see, an off-peak first checked bag on a domestic flight will now cost you $50-60 (depending on whether you pay in advance), while a peak first checked bag on a domestic flight will now cost you $55-70 (depending on whether you pay in advance). For context, below are the dates that are considered peak for the purposes of bag fees.
It goes without saying that paying $50-70 for a first checked bag is a pretty substantial cost, especially when you consider how little checked bags used to cost. On a one-way, you’re looking at $100-140. For a family of four, you’d be looking at $400-560.
When JetBlue raised checked bag fees earlier this year, the airline released a statement claiming it was increasing checked bag fees to be “more competitive,” and that “while we recognize that fee increases are never ideal, we take careful consideration to ensure these changes are implemented only when necessary.” I imagine this time around, the logic is much of the same.
The simple reality is that oil prices are way up. Airlines have actually done a solid job of being able to make fare increases stick. But that’s not enough to fully offset the increase in the cost of jet fuel.
JetBlue is in a rough financial spot, and it hasn’t turned a profit since before the pandemic. The airline is hoping to turn an operating profit in 2027 , though that strikes me as being particularly optimistic. So the logic for raising checked bags is threefold:
JetBlue has just increased checked bag fees once again, and you’ll now pay $50-70 for a first checked bag on a domestic flight. This is JetBlue’s second price increase on checked bags so far this year. When airlines are trying to increase revenue, checked bag fees are often low hanging fruit.
When competitors match, it also becomes something that’s unavoidable for consumers, other than getting a credit card… which also has upside for the airline! I’d be shocked if other airlines don’t match this move from JetBlue.

articles.title_orig: Hackers behind $6.3bn Binance heist ‘used malware and bogus job interviews’
articles.title_zh: Hackers behind $6.3bn Binance heist ‘used malware and bogus job interviews’
articles.content_orig:
Firm reveals details about how its cryptocurrency exchange was compromised, saying operation began in June
The hackers behind the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) Binance heist used bogus job interviews, malicious software and an internal AI tool, the company has revealed.
The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange was compromised in an operation that began with an inadvertent download of malware in June, led to a recruitment scam in September and then a raid last week of “hot wallets” where billions of dollars worth of crypto-assets were taken.
The FBI has blamed North Korea for last week’s heist but Pyongyang, a prolific crypto-hacker , described the accusation as “absurd rhetoric” on Tuesday.
According to an update Binance released on Tuesday, the hackers got their first foothold in the summer when a company engineer inadvertently downloaded malware that exposed the employee’s role and that of others in the team that looked after Binance’s cryptowallet infrastructure.
A fake project director then contacted a different engineer on a legitimate job-hunting platform, leading to a first-round video interview with a sham HR representative and a second-round interview – on a chat app – with the “chief executive” of a fictitious company. It was during the second interview that the engineer was tricked into downloading malware on to his computer.
On 20 October, the attacker used the compromised computer plus an internal AI tool to gain control of the engineer’s system and that of a second wallet developer on the same team. Then on 29 October, the attacker used the second developer’s computer, using stolen ⁠credentials from the first engineer, and triggered a malicious script to ​launch the attack.
Binance said $2.85bn of the $6.34bn drained from cryptowallets in the attack had been frozen or intercepted.
Deepfake job interviews are a known part of North Korea’s cyber-arsenal , but normally from the other side of the process – where bogus IT professionals apply for jobs as a means of funnelling money back to Pyongyang.
“This should not have happened, and we apologise for the concern, disruption and uncertainty it caused our users, partners and the wider industry,” Binance said in the update.
The FBI said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the hack.
after newsletter promotion
But Kim Yo-jong, the influential sister of the North Korean leader Kim Jong-un , said on Tuesday that the allegations proved Washington remained hostile towards Pyongyang, according to North Korea’s state news agency, KCNA.
“The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK [the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea] as a ‘cybercriminal state,’ claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organisation ‘supported’ by the DPRK was involved in the incident,” KCNA quoted her as saying.
“But the US assertion ‌is absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” said Kim, a ruling party official.
“It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads international public opinion as if all the cybercrimes in different parts of the world are our deeds.”

articles.title_orig: China seeks APEC solutions to world development ahead of leaders’ summit
articles.title_zh: China seeks APEC solutions to world development ahead of leaders’ summit
articles.content_orig:
China on Tuesday urged Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) members to continue contributing practical and effective "Asia-Pacific solutions" to the region's and the world's development, according to media reports.
Top diplomat Wang Yi highlighted the importance of the upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting later this month in an address to the 37th Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Ministerial Meeting via video conference, state-run Xinhua News reported.
Wang, who co-chaired the meeting with Commerce Minister Wang Wentao, said Beijing is willing to work with "all parties" to do a "good job" in the final stage of the 2026 APEC "China Year" and contribute to the fruitful results at the leaders' meeting.
He said the leaders' meeting is an "important one" concerning the future development of the Asia-Pacific region.
The commerce minister urged all APEC parties to uphold free trade and innovation-driven development, foster a vibrant engine for growth, advance discussions and policy coordination on digital and intelligent economic and trade rules, and build a fair and equitable international economic and trade order.
China will host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in south China in November. It will mark the country's third time hosting the event, following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014.
The theme of the summit is "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together.” China has identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priority areas for this year's APEC cooperation.

articles.title_orig: iOS 27.3 introduces new iPhone Duo feature for one-handed use
articles.title_zh: iOS 27.3 introduces new iPhone Duo feature for one-handed use
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27.3 beta 1 launched today with a variety of new features, including a big upgrade for one-handed iPhone Duo use thanks to Reachability.
When iPhone Duo reviews first arrived last month, some complained that the extra-wide design of the outer display made it difficult to use one-handed.
At the time, Apple said that it would introduce Reachability via a future software update to help.
Today with iOS 27.3 beta 1, Reachability has officially arrived for iPhone Duo users.
Unlike Reachability on other iPhones, which shifts the screen down vertically, the iPhone Duo version works horizontally.
Once the feature is enabled (Settings ⇾ Accessibility ⇾ Reachability), a short swipe to the side of the screen will shift everything to the left or right, making it easier to reach.
If you’re struggling at all with one-handed iPhone Duo use, iOS 27.3 might make a big difference.
Currently iOS 27.3 is only available in developer beta, but a public beta is expected to launch in the coming days. However, if you’re concerned about bugs or performance issues, we recommend waiting for the launch version. Apple has said that iOS 27.3 will ship to all users next month, with mid-December the most likely window.
Have you tried Reachability on iPhone Duo yet? How is it working for you? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title_orig: Siri AI Gets More Capable in iOS 27.3
articles.title_zh: Siri AI Gets More Capable in iOS 27.3
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27 just made your iPhone a lot more capable.
The iPhone is easy to recommend to anyone looking for great smartphone hardware and long-term software support. The previous few iOS releases, however, have been pretty janky. With iOS 27, Apple therefore shifted its focus to ironing out bugs and improving overall stability rather than cramming in another round of flashy new features, and a good chunk of the WWDC 2026 keynote covered improvements such as snappier app launch times, faster AirDrop transfers and better memory management.
Apple's commitment to software updates also means iOS 27 compatibility extends all the way back to the iPhone 11, which is great news since iOS 26 would have been a terrible final major update to be stuck on. If you haven't already updated your iPhone, you can do so by navigating to Settings > General > Software Update .
Not much has changed visually, which makes sense since Apple only recently overhauled its design language with Liquid Glass. There is now a system-wide transparency slider, though, which many users had been asking about. Reports about battery life are mixed — some say they're getting less screen-on time than before, while others haven't had issues. Personally, iOS 27 has been such a blessing performance-wise on my aging iPhone 15 Pro Max that I'm willing to put up with slightly worse battery life.
Of course, stability upgrades aren't the only thing Apple introduced with iOS 27. The update also brings a handful of useful tidbits, and here are five features you should definitely check out after updating your iPhone.
Apple Intelligence has had a rocky start. After all, it took Apple two whole iOS generations to deliver on its promises of a more capable Siri. Most of the Apple Intelligence suite has been pretty underwhelming, unless you're one of the five people who enjoy generating custom emojis using Genmoji , but iOS 27 changes that. The Shortcuts app has received a major upgrade, and Apple Intelligence might finally have a genuinely useful feature to show for itself.
You've been able to create pretty complex shortcuts and automations on iOS for a while now, and you can even import shortcuts that others have created and shared. iOS 27 now lets you create shortcuts using natural language prompts, which Apple Intelligence handles. When you launch the app and tap the + button, you can start describing the shortcut you want.
In my testing, the integration works pretty well and usually creates straightforward shortcuts without issues. That said, it pieces together the wrong actions sometimes and ends up with a shortcut that doesn't do exactly what you want. Fortunately, you can still manually tweak shortcuts created using Apple Intelligence by tapping Edit .
You can also use Apple Intelligence actions within your shortcuts. Apple currently offers three AI models, including an on-device model for faster processing. You can create shortcuts for actions involving information extraction, summarization or generation of text and documents. The Cloud and Cloud Pro models do have a daily rate limit, though.
The Wallet app on the iPhone stores your payment cards, transit passes, event and cinema tickets, digital keys and more. Until now, users could only add digital passes and credentials if the issuer supported Apple Wallet and provided a compatible pass. While several companies and services offered this convenience, plenty of issuers didn't support it. As a collector, I was a bit disheartened to see my local IMAX theater stop offering Apple Wallet passes for movie tickets.
With iOS 27, you can create custom passes and add them to Apple Wallet. This is extremely handy for those with loyalty cards or gym memberships that don't offer native Apple Wallet support. There are two ways you can create a pass in Apple Wallet, and Apple Intelligence comes in handy again here. On supported iPhone models, you can open an image (or screenshot) of a ticket or membership card with a barcode, swipe up and tap on Add Pass to Wallet .
If this option doesn't show up, you can also open the Wallet app, tap the + icon at the top and select Create a Pass . Tap on Continue and take a photo of the ticket or ID card. The Wallet app will then use Visual Intelligence to extract relevant information from the image and create a pass. If you want to change the pass' details or visuals, tap Edit.
For years, Apple's virtual assistant, Siri, has lagged behind competitors like Google Assistant. Slow responses are forgivable, but Siri would often struggle with even the most basic requests. Apple first promised a major Siri overhaul with iOS 18's Apple Intelligence suite, but it's taken over two years to come to fruition. iOS 27 comes with Siri AI , and users with a compatible iPhone can join the waitlist by navigating to Settings > Siri . The AI-powered virtual assistant is still in beta, but things are already starting to look promising.
Siri now understands and fulfills your requests noticeably better, with a huge improvement in how it handles follow-up queries. Though it still takes a hot second to process most requests, its responses are more relevant, and it doesn't hit you with the "Here's what I found on the web" reply as often. What's more impressive about Siri AI, though, is the fact that it now understands personal context.
It can pull information from your messages, emails, photos and more to answer questions or perform tasks that previously required you to manually dig through different apps. Third-party app support is still limited, but if you mainly use iMessage and the default Mail app on your iPhone, you'll likely find Siri to be one of iOS 27's biggest improvements. The Camera app has a new Siri mode as well, which taps into Visual Intelligence to answer questions about whatever you're pointing your camera at.
The AirPods are some of the most popular wireless earbuds on the market, and they work best when paired with an iPhone, iPad or Mac. Most modern AirPods models support Spatial Audio with head tracking, and several music streaming services like Apple Music and Tidal let you enjoy Dolby Atmos content. Sound quality is also widely regarded as one of their strongest selling points, particularly on the higher-end Pro models like the AirPods Pro 3 that we reviewed. With iOS 27, though, you can finally tweak the sound to your liking using a built-in equalizer.
Apps like Apple Music have long allowed you to apply EQ presets, but the new AirPods equalizer works system-wide. The feature is available on AirPods 4 and newer, AirPods Pro 2 and newer and the AirPods Max 2. Connect your AirPods to your iPhone, launch the Settings app, tap on the AirPods settings at the top of the screen and navigate to Audio & Routing > Equalizer .
The Recommended option is selected by default, which delivers the balanced sound profile you've grown used to. If you tap on Custom , you can manually adjust the lows, mids and highs to your liking. If you prefer thumpy bass, increase the lows slider, but if you want vocals to sound clearer, try bumping up the mids or highs instead. Though Apple is only offering a 3-band equalizer, it's still a welcome addition. My AirPods Pro 2 already deliver punchy lows, but as a basshead, I appreciate having the option to crank up the bass even further.
Apple's latest mobile OS also has several additions that make browsing more convenient. For starters, Safari now lets you set up alerts for webpage changes, so you don't have to check yourself. This is useful if you're tracking a product's price, waiting for tickets to go on sale or keeping an eye on when an out-of-stock item becomes available again.
On your iPhone, launch Safari , head to a webpage you want to track, tap on the icon with three horizontal lines in the address bar and select Notify Me . Since this feature uses Apple Intelligence, you can describe what exactly you want Safari to monitor. You can then choose how frequently Safari checks the webpage for changes.

articles.title_orig: iOS 27.3 Adds Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode to Safari
articles.title_zh: iOS 27.3 Adds Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode to Safari
articles.content_orig:
With iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS Golden Gate 27.3, Apple is making major updates to Safari. The browser is getting a Vertical Tabs layout, which can be used instead of the standard horizontal tab bar. It's a change that pairs well with the iPhone Duo 's larger display, but it is available across iPhone, iPad , and Mac.
Vertical Tabs are located on the left side of the display and use icons by default to save space, but there is an option to make the tab bar wider to show website titles as well. Vertical Tabs work with both Topics and Tab Groups to keep things organized. Topics are created when automatic Apple Intelligence tab sorting is turned on in iOS 27 . Pinning tabs by dragging, quickly swapping between Tab Groups, and other features also continue to work.
The option to turn on Vertical Tabs is located in the Safari settings or in the View menu on Mac and ‌iPad‌.
Apple is adding Adaptive Dark Mode for websites that don't have a dark mode design option by default. If you use ‌Dark Mode‌ and then browse to a website with a bright background color, Safari will offer an option to "Try" Adaptive ‌Dark Mode‌.
After tapping Try, Safari renders a ‌Dark Mode‌ version of the page that makes the background darker, changes text contrast, inverts logos and graphics, recolors vector artwork, lifts raised surfaces, and rebalances layered shadows. Each website will be adapted based on what's needed to make it readable, so not every tweak is applied to every site. You can opt to turn Adaptive ‌Dark Mode‌ on for all sites or on a site-by-site basis after using it.
If a site has a native dark mode or has a dark design already, Adaptive ‌Dark Mode‌ won't activate. Developers can also add a tag that causes Safari to ignore Adaptive ‌Dark Mode‌ and show the website as the developer intended.
Along with these visual changes, Apple is adding new Siri AI actions. ‌Siri‌ can take action on tabs and windows, sorting, moving, closing, and arranging in Tab Groups. ‌Siri‌ also has control over web history, and you can ask it to clear your history for a particular site and for a set time period, such as the last 10 days.
‌Siri‌ can already see what's on your screen, but soon, ‌Siri‌ will also be able to understand the full content of webpages, including non-active tabs and content not in view. You will be able to ask questions about information across websites, so if you have multiple tabs open when shopping for an item, ‌Siri‌ will be able to sort them by price or give you information on the product that you're looking at. Apple says the ‌Siri‌ awareness feature is coming, but it's not in the first beta.
The changes to Safari are available for developers starting today in the latest betas. An Apple Intelligence-capable device is required for the ‌Siri‌ features.
iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ 27.3 will launch this December after several rounds of beta testing to refine the new features.

articles.title_orig: What the midterm elections could mean for markets, debt
articles.title_zh: What the midterm elections could mean for markets, debt
articles.content_orig:
‘Varney & Co.’ host Stuart Varney examines a potential socialist surge, Republican upsets in red states and what an election shakeup could mean for Congress and Wall Street.
Voters across America are casting their ballots in the midterm elections on Tuesday, which will determine control of Congress and could add to investors' concerns about oversight of the artificial intelligence (AI) sector and how the debt ceiling will be addressed next year.
Since President Donald Trump's second term began in 2025 with Republican majorities in both chambers of Congress, the S&P 500 has gained about 27% in part due to a massive influx of spending on AI and strong earnings growth.
Treasury yields are also significantly higher in part because of geopolitical risks that emerged with the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, which caused a surge in energy prices. U.S. budget deficits have continued to widen to about $2 trillion, adding more upward pressure to yields as debt issuance mounts.
Investors are weighing how the results of the election will affect the outlook for financial markets depending on whether Democrats take control of one or both chambers of Congress.
AFFORDABILITY TAKES CENTER STAGE AS AMERICANS CAST THEIR BALLOTS IN HIGH-STAKES MIDTERMS
The midterm elections will determine control of Congress for the next two years, carrying implications for the nation's finances and markets. (J. David Ake/Getty Images)
Since 1930, there have been eight midterm cycles when the president's party lost control of the House, and the S&P 500 rose for the remainder of the year five times, Ned Davis Research said. It posted a median gain of 1.4% from Election Day through year-end, slightly less than the 1.9% posted across all post-Election Day midterm years.
In a scenario in which Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress , investors expect tougher oversight of AI which could weigh on markets that have been pushed higher by the emerging tech.
Democratic majorities would have the ability to investigate corporate America while attempting to slow deregulation , which could increase market volatility.
DSA PLATFORM COULD COST UP TO $212T OVER A DECADE, ANALYSIS FINDS
Markets have generally fared well under divided government. (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
If Democrats win the House but Republicans hold their majority in the Senate, implications for the U.S. fiscal situation could be mixed.
Bipartisan compromises would be required over issues like funding the government to avoid shutdowns and raising the debt ceiling , which could create the potential for brinkmanship.
In a scenario where Republicans retain their majorities in the House and Senate, the GOP could pursue further tax reforms or boost defense spending.
FEDERAL BUDGET DEFICIT HITS $2T AS NATIONAL DEBT COSTS SURGE
The results of the midterms will impact negotiations between Congress and the Trump administration depending on who controls the House and Senate. (Grant Baldwin/AFP via Getty Images)
Ned Davis chief U.S. strategist Ed Clissold said that a House takeover by Democrats could modestly temper the U.S. equity market's year-end rally, but in general it hasn't prevented stocks from advancing.
"Conventional wisdom is that gridlock is good (for stocks)," said Clissold, adding that stocks have performed better under Democratic presidents than Republicans.
Diego Barnuevo, market analyst at Ebury, said that a Democratic-held Congress' negotiations with the White House would likely be limited to the budget and debt ceiling, and that a "Democratic sweep would be neutral to mildly positive for the fiscal outlook."

articles.title_orig: Google Curbs AI in School Accounts After Pushback
articles.title_zh: Google Curbs AI in School Accounts After Pushback
articles.content_orig:
We’re bringing Guided Learning capabilities to Search and Google Classroom, and evolving our approach to school controls.
VP & General Manager, Education
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Chris Phillips, VP and General Manager of Education, is introducing Guided Learning to Google Search and Google Classroom to help students think critically through complex problems. These tools provide step-by-step coaching instead of direct answers to support productive study habits. You can find Guided Learning in Google Classroom today, and we are beginning a pilot program for Search in select U.S. schools later this month.
Chris Phillips, VP and General Manager of Education, explains that we are adding Guided Learning to Google Search and Classroom to help students think through problems instead of just finding quick answers. This tool acts like a personal coach, using questions to guide students through complex topics step by step. We are also giving school administrators full control to decide which AI tools are available to their students, ensuring technology supports classroom learning.
If you’ve ever watched a student use AI tools to help with their schoolwork, you’ve probably wondered: Are they actually learning, or just finding a shortcut? Questions like this are important, and they guide our work when building products for learning.
We believe technology paired with great educators can unlock incredible learning potential, and we’re focused on building technology responsibly to help students thrive. Today, we’re making important updates to our products used in schools, including building Guided Learning capabilities into Google Search and Google Classroom, and evolving our approach to school controls.
We believe AI products should support “productive struggle” — enabling students to be actively challenged without getting so overwhelmed that they give up. That’s the philosophy behind Guided Learning. In Gemini, Guided Learning acts as an interactive study tool that coaches students through the process of problem solving through open-ended questions and step-by-step breakdowns. Our research shows that Guided Learning leads to measurable learning gains for students, and we’re now bringing Guided Learning to more products.
Google Classroom: Starting today, Guided Learning is globally available in Google Classroom, a central hub where teachers and students organize schoolwork, share assignments and stay connected. When a student starts a Guided Learning activity assigned by their teacher, it acts like a 1-1 study tool, anchored in class material to help them stay on task. It also gives teachers real-time insights to spot where the class might need extra support.
Before launching Guided Learning in Google Classroom, we worked closely with schools and educators to test the feature and integrate their feedback.
We believe schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach. After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.
We’ll share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition. Our goal is simple: provide school leaders the control and confidence to use AI products in classrooms as they see fit.
We’ll continue to listen to feedback and evolve our approach as we work in partnership with schools, teachers, pedagogical experts, and parents on helping the next generation learn and thrive.

articles.title_orig: Google to shut off search for schools that opt out of AI
articles.title_zh: Google to shut off search for schools that opt out of AI
articles.content_orig:
Google announced Tuesday morning that it would switch off AI products by default for students in schools that use the technology giant’s education software. But those schools that forgo its AI services would also be cut off from Google Search.
The move comes after mounting criticism from advocacy groups and senators about the spread of Google’s AI services available in classrooms. Until Tuesday, its AI products — branded under the Gemini moniker — were automatically activated for schools using Google Classroom.
Google said Tuesday’s move would also cut off students’ access to Google Search if schools do not enable Gemini, given AI’s growing integration into the company’s search products.
Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president and general manager of education, said in a blog post announcing the change that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search “will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.”
“We believe schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach,” Phillips wrote.
Some education and technology advocates immediately slammed the decision, painting the move as a punishment for schools that don’t use Google’s AI. “It is unfortunate that Google has prioritized its business interests over the education of our children,” said Randi Weingarten, president of the American Federation of Teachers, a national educators union.
“Instead of working with teachers and parents to uphold privacy and ensure their tools are safe and useful, it throws the baby out with the bathwater and bans access to the tools altogether,” she told NBC News in written comments.
Josh Golin, executive director of advocacy group Fairplay, said in a statement that Google is attempting “to strong-arm schools into using its AI products.”
“Schools should use this opportunity to help students find more privacy-protective alternatives for search, as well as ways to do more substantive research beyond search and click,” Golin said.
In a statement posted to social media after this article was published, Google said the announcements “give schools more choice, not less,” and that schools can turn on Google Search individually without enabling Gemini products. But Search will still have AI features built into it, which the company said have been updated “to make it better for learning. Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.”
Earlier this year, Google turned on Gemini in its Classroom app, allowing children — regardless of age — to access AI products unless districts disabled it .
Parent advocacy groups and experts on the use of technology in schools denounced Google for providing AI products to children — raising concern that students would outsource their work to AI systems on school devices — and lobbied school districts to disable Gemini products. In an open letter in early October, 13 leading parent advocacy organizations — including the Digital Childhood Institute and Schools Beyond Screens — called on school districts to turn off access to Gemini and YouTube, which is also owned by Google .
Google has established a dominant role in education technology over the past 15 years. The vast majority of Chromebook laptops are purchased by school districts to provide to students. Nearly two-thirds of assignments use a Google product, according to a 2023 report by the firm Schoolytics. This year, the company began offering multiday AI trainings for educators, featuring sessions that focused on how they could mitigate pushback by teachers who don’t want to use AI.
Research on AI in educational settings has not established a long-term benefit for students. There are no high-quality causal studies into student use of AI, according to the SCALE Initiative at the Stanford Graduate School of Education . Researchers have also warned that many of the studies conducted so far on AI in education didn’t measure whether it boosted learning and often did not test whether AI-assisted learning was superior to other teaching methods.
In Tuesday’s blog post , Google said that for schools that enable the company’s AI products, they will now detect when a student is trying to use them just to get an answer on an assignment. A redesigned version of Google Search will instead walk students through the topic or problem and work through the concepts, without going directly to the answer, the company said.
Jared Perlo is a technology reporter focused on AI for NBC News Digital.
Tyler Kingkade is a national reporter for NBC News, based in Los Angeles.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
articles.title_zh: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
articles.content_orig:
ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI.
ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI.
In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.
Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.)
Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade. During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree. (OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in-house search index, although there is still some speculation that it routes some queries through Google.)
The news comes amid an ongoing search engine shake-up, as Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third-party sites and invests heavily in AI tools — not just AI Overview but also additional generative AI capabilities , including personalized search results with visualizations and charts. But as search queries increasingly route through OpenAI and other AI labs’ services, other companies are investing in the same types of AI-focused search experience, even if they call it something else: for OpenAI, it’s “Intelligent UI,” or creating a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response. “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” Fry said.
Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year. OpenAI has defended its ads in the past, and Fry told reporters they hadn’t produced a lasting backlash. “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” he said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.”
OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before.
“Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.

articles.title_orig: Former Weil partners lawyer up over firm’s wind-down

articles.content_orig:
By Legal Cheek on Nov 3 2026 10:32am
11 outfits take steps, including adjusting application processes, to support future trainees left in limbo
A group of leading US and City law firms are stepping in to support future trainees whose training contracts with Weil will no longer go ahead following the firm’s decision to wind down its operations.
Many of those affected are already partway through their studies, including the SQE, and now face the daunting prospect of having to secure a training contract elsewhere, despite having already successfully navigated the competitive recruitment process.
According to Financial News (£) , 11 law firms have so far offered their support, citing a person familiar with the matter. They are Akin , Baker McKenzie , Debevoise , Jones Day , Kirkland & Ellis , Latham & Watkins , Macfarlanes , Paul, Weiss , Skadden, Sullivan & Cromwell and Willkie .
The support on offer varies between firms but includes streamlining training contract applications by removing certain stages and allowing affected candidates to submit their CVs directly. More are expected to follow suit in the coming weeks as Weil’s graduate recruitment team continues discussions with other outfits, the report adds.
The Legal Cheek Firms Most List 2027 shows that Weil recruits approximately 15 trainees each year, offering a starting salary of £60,000 and covering the costs of students’ law conversion courses and SQE preparation.
Weil announced last week that its management committee had recommended an “ orderly wind-down “, bringing months of senior departures , unsuccessful merger discussions and leadership uncertainty to a head. The New York-founded firm has around 1,200 lawyers globally and has been in business for more than 90 years.
The proposal is expected to go before partners for a vote in the coming days, with the firm saying it would continue supporting staff during the closure process.
Reminds me of the KWM days!
So the support is, for your sins we will make our overly protracted recruitment processes, slightly less protracted for you. That’s grand.
Genuinely honking offer of help
This whole ‘save the lawyers’ thing irks me. Yes it sucks to lose your job but so what if the world loses some aspiring corporate lawyers. Not like they’re top brain surgeons is it…
And the fact that those who are picked up get to bypass other firm’s notoriously selective recruitment processes annoys me. What if they dont gel with your culture or dont actually like your key areas (admittedly a lot of similarity)?

articles.title_orig: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
articles.title_zh: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
articles.content_orig:
The New York Times and other newspaper companies sued Brave Software yesterday, alleging that the browser maker illegally bypasses paywalls and sells stolen news content to AI companies.
“Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere,” the NYT alleged in a lawsuit filed in US District Court for the Southern District of New York. Citing third-party revenue estimates, the suit claimed that “Brave has made more than $100 million by copying and reselling publishers’ work without consent or permission,” while “publishers have received nothing.”
The lawsuit said, “AI companies pay Brave to provide them with real-time online content from the Brave search index,” and use content from the Brave index “to train their own AI models” and “to respond to specific user queries.” The NYT lawsuit points to Brave’s website , which says the Brave Search API is “used by some of the biggest names in AI, including Cohere, Mistral, Perplexity, and You.com.”
The lawsuit accused Brave of all the major types of copyright infringement: direct infringement, contributory infringement, and vicarious infringement. The lawsuit claims Brave infringes copyrights directly by scraping articles for its search index, for its “Ask Brave” AI search feature, and for the Brave API that “serves as an illicit source of unlicensed copyrighted material, including Times journalism, to other AI companies.”
The NYT accused Brave of being “a contributory and vicarious infringer when it deliberately induces, facilitates, controls, and profits from its users’ and GenAI customers’ copying of the copyrighted content.” Finally, the lawsuit said Brave violated the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) by circumventing technological measures the NYT and other content owners use to restrict access to their articles.
“The Brave Browser includes a default setting that, when activated, causes the browser to go behind website paywalls and provide the paywalled content to the user,” the lawsuit said. The browser “blocks advertising that would otherwise appear on The Times’s website, and instead shows its own ads, offering its users a cut of the revenue even as it deprives The Times of digital advertising revenue that helps it fund the expensive effort of producing journalism,” the lawsuit said.
When testing the Brave browser for Mac today, we found that the optional “paywall blocker” feature made it possible to read a paywalled New York Times article. The feature was enabled in the default settings and can be turned off.
The NYT asked for a permanent injunction to stop Brave from continuing the allegedly illegal conduct. The lawsuit seeks statutory damages, actual damages, restitution of profits derived from alleged copyright infringement, and “restitution and disgorgement of all revenue and profits Brave obtained through its ad-substitution scheme.”
A similar lawsuit was filed against Brave in the same court yesterday by the New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune, and Orlando Sentinel companies. We contacted Brave and will update this article if it provides a response.
Perplexity, which is not a defendant in the Brave lawsuit but is facing a different lawsuit filed by the NYT, accused the news organization of “disinformation” in a statement provided to Ars and other news outlets. Perplexity’s statement did not identify any specific inaccuracies in the lawsuit against Brave.
“The New York Times is overpaying its attorneys and underpaying its journalists. (Who could’ve easily identified the disinformation in this suit.),” Perplexity’s statement said.
The NYT sued Perplexity in December 2025, alleging that its AI tool gives users “outputs that are identical or substantially similar to” NYT articles, including “verbatim or near-verbatim reproductions, summaries, or abridgements of the original content.” Perplexity’s response to that lawsuit said its answer engine only fetches content from copyrighted articles in reply to user queries. Perplexity argued that “developing an AI tool that can allegedly automatically fetch and provide specific content in response to user requests based on its pre-configuration and access to materials available on the Internet” is not “volitional conduct.”
The NYT also sued OpenAI and Microsoft in December 2023 in a lawsuit alleging that OpenAI trains its AI with stolen news content. The lawsuit is heading toward a trial , with OpenAI arguing that its use of news articles is fair use under copyright law.
